pure-announcement.rationale: It is a data briefing aggregating third-party scans, CVEs and surveys, not a launch or release note — the embedded certification pitch is framing, not the substance.

duplicate.rationale: The corpus's MCP security concepts (authorization hardening, shadow MCP detection, remote-first governance) cover techniques and spec changes, not this body of incident and vulnerability statistics.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Nearly every figure is attributed to a named source — JFrog, Endor Labs, Astrix, Gartner, CVE identifiers — that a reader can check.

durability.rationale: The substance is adoption counts, scan percentages and CVE lists pinned to 2025–2026 — a snapshot that will be stale within a year, even though the attack-class taxonomy and the adoption-outpaced-security pattern persist.

actionability.rationale: It describes the threat landscape in numbers but prescribes nothing beyond buying the vendor's certification; a builder gets urgency from it, not a practice.

atomicity.rationale: Ten loosely-joined statistic categories — adoption, vuln classes, CVEs, registry audits, incidents, supply chain, API stats, bounties, surveys — serve one thesis but do not reduce to one paragraph without discarding most of the note.
